# Single-page app

*Concept* · also written single-page apps · single-page application · single-page applications · SPA · SPAs

A website that loads one page and swaps content with JavaScript, which needs real URLs and status codes to be indexed well.

**Glossary** (*Single-page app (SPA)*): A JavaScript application that changes views without full page reloads. Typical search risks: links without real URLs, # routes and error views that return 200.

Narrative: the topic [JavaScript SEO pitfalls and fixes](../topics/javascript-seo.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

12 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 7 shown or said at the event (5 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 3 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics).

- [`D2-C192`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google's JavaScript guides say that when client-side routing makes a real 404 status impractical, a single-page app can avoid soft 404s by redirecting with JavaScript to a URL whose server returns 404, or by adding a robots noindex meta tag with JavaScript. `[D2-C192, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C294`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Docs: For client-side rendered single-page apps, where meaningful status codes can be impossible or impractical, Google's documentation gives two ways to avoid soft 404s: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns a 404 status, or a noindex robots meta tag added with JavaScript. `[D2-C294, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C185`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The crawlable pattern for single-page app navigation is a real URL in the href, such as `<a href=/products>`, combined with History API routing (window.history.pushState) instead of hash routes. `[D2-C185, slide, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C190`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: In single-page apps, a missing page often shows a custom 404 page while the server returns HTTP 200, because the front-end router, not the server, handles the 404. `[D2-C190, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C285`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google recommends the History API to give single-page apps clean URLs instead of fragment-based routes. `[D2-C285, slide, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C288`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: With the History API, a single-page app can use real links and attach event listeners that intercept the click, rewrite the URL with pushState and load the new content, so Google can follow the links while users avoid full page reloads. `[D2-C288, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C291`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: In JavaScript single-page apps, soft 404s typically arise because the server returns the app with a 200 status for every URL, so when the app shows a 'not found' message for a URL that does not exist, no error is reported. `[D2-C291, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C286`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Moving a single-page app from fragment-based routes to real paths with the History API keeps the same client-side behaviour and was described as not free but relatively straightforward. `[D2-C286, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C183`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: A community speaker listed four common but often overlooked JavaScript rendering mistakes: non-crawlable link markup, error pages that return HTTP 200 in single-page apps, content behind user interaction, and JavaScript or API resources blocked in robots.txt. `[D2-C183, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C193`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: In a single-page app, let the server return 404 for unknown routes where possible; otherwise use one of the two client-side fixes Google documents for error views: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns 404, or a robots noindex added with JavaScript. `[D2-C193, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C290`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Analysis: Audit a single-page app by searching both the templates and the rendered HTML for href="#..." routes, `<a>` elements without href and onclick navigation; every view that should rank needs an `<a href>` link to a real path. `[D2-C290, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C342`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: Return real error status codes for error states, 404 or 410 for missing content and 503 for outages such as a failed database connection, also in single-page apps; a 200 page whose main content is only an error message is treated as a soft 404 even when header and navigation look normal. `[D2-C342, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-ERR-02` **MUST** · Documented: Return a real 404 for unknown routes in single-page apps, or use a documented client-side fallback (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-PRF-04` **SHOULD** · Documented: Keep each HTML response well under 2 MB and put the main content and JSON-LD early (its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-02` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not navigate with onclick handlers, javascript: URLs, routerLink without href or # pseudo-links (its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-03` **MUST** · Documented: Route single-page apps with the History API and real paths, not # fragments (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
